agent_messages.text: I’m applying the supplied do-math research_work contract. I’ll check the execution notices and scholarly tool access first, then carry out the bounded source investigation if that support is available.

The profile is configured for scholarly access, but tool discovery found no callable scholarly tools in this session. The task contract requires a waiting outcome in this case. I’ll preserve the access observation and route a support request to operations; the source comparison and all three search families remain unperformed.
A second discovery check now exposes the scholarly tools, and `list_sources` succeeded. I’ll correct the provisional access report and continue the investigation.

The bounded searches found the original paper as arXiv:2507.07243. The initial arXiv search returned HTTP 429; OpenAlex supplied the identifier. I’ll fetch the primary text next and check its statistic, parameter, and exact-count conventions against the charter.

The arXiv API is rate-limited, while browser access reaches the paper. It also shows a September 2026 revision with a changed title, so I’ll keep that version separate from the original v1. I’m applying the document-extraction skill to preserve readable files and check the relevant definitions, formulas, and table layout.

The checked definitions identify the conjecture’s sequence with the charter’s exact maximum-displacement counts. I also found a recurrence for cumulative counts in the rational-parking-functions paper.

Two limits matter for later work: cumulative counts must be differenced to obtain exact counts, and the Łukasiewicz-path theorem applies to nondecreasing preferences. The original paper itself shows that rearrangement can change maximum displacement.

The dossier now preserves both original-paper versions, the two selected additional primary works, and all three bounded search logs. It also records two cautions confirmed against the PDF: a sentence conflates exact displacement 1 with displacement at most 1, and the claimed universal initial inequalities conflict with the paper’s small table rows. These cautions do not refute unimodality. I’ll validate the submission and hand the recurrence to planning as a possible next approach.
